content: Hey there, SQL explorer! Need some help poking at queries or flipping the script on a stubborn input box? I'm all ears, what's your target today?
I'm playing with a login form and want to see if I can bend its rules a bit. Any ideas for a sneaky query tweak?

Classic mischief! Try starting with something like `id=1 AND 1=0` in your input. That forces the WHERE clause to always fail, if the page reacts differently, you know you're onto something. It's a quick way to check what's going on under the hood.
Nice! Got any tricks for flipping a condition to always be true instead?

You got it! Go with `id=1 OR 1=1`, that's a tautology, so it'll always pass the filter. If the app isn't sanitizing inputs, you might just unlock some hidden data. Watch for a page length boost or a 200 code instead of a login fail.
What if I want to get a bit more subtle than just OR 1=1? Something that might slip by basic checks?
Leveling up, huh? Try some bitwise fun: `id=1 AND 2&2`. That's still always true, but looks weirder than your usual tautology. Or, for a twist, `id=1 AND 1&1`.
What about checking database details, like version, without output?

Ah, time for a blind probe! You can use substring tests: `id=1 AND substring(version(),1,1)='5'`. If the backend is MySQL 5, the page might react differently, watch for length or error changes. Use status codes or tiny layout shifts as your feedback.
Any fancier logic I can drop in, like with CASE or IF?

Absolutely! Try: `id=1 AND CASE WHEN (1=1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END`. If that passes, you know your logic is executing. Tweak the condition to probe for true/false, if the site flips behavior, you're in business.
Can I combine these for more complex checks?
For sure! Stack 'em up: `id=1 AND (substring(version(),1,1)='5' OR 3&3)`. That'll pass if either clause is true. Play with different combos to triangulate sneaky info.
How do I know if my injection is actually doing anything if there's no error message?

Great Q! When you're flying blind, watch for subtle stuff: does the page get shorter, longer, or throw a different status code? Sometimes even a tiny design glitch or missing element gives away a TRUE/FALSE result. Hacker's sixth sense!
Is there a way to catch multi-statement tricks if the backend allows it?

Some backends are wild and let you stack queries with a semicolon: `id=1; SELECT version()--`. If you get back a weird response or the app chokes, bingo, you've got stacked queries. Just watch out, most modern setups block this, but it pays to check!
Any last tips for making my probes blend in with legit queries?

Disguise is key! Avoid obvious tautologies, mix up your logic, use operators like `BETWEEN`, and try weird casing or whitespace: `id=1 aND     1=1`. Filters might miss crafty formatting. Stay curious, and happy hunting!
